BMW's Battery Deals Land as Guidance Cuts and a 721,000-Car Recall Test Investor Nerve
sum: BMW has locked in Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution to supply its Gen6 high-voltage battery cells, with the Korean pair splitting duties by region: Samsung SDI covering Europe and LG Energy Solution handling the United States. Deliveries from those regional plants are slated to begin from the end of the 2020s, the company said.
The supply agreements, finalised on Monday, give the Munich-based automaker a measure of certainty on its next-generation electric drivetrain just as its near-term numbers have come under pressure.

For the third quarter of 2026, BMW reported group revenue of EUR 30.452 billion (EUR 30.5 billion) and a pre-tax group result of EUR 2.083 billion (EUR 2.08 billion). The automotive segment's EBIT margin came in at 3.4%. Deliveries, however, slipped 6.3% year on year to roughly 551,000 vehicles.

The company has since slashed its full-year outlook for the automotive EBIT margin to a range of ?0.5% to +0.5%, down from the 1% to 3% it had previously guided. Return on capital employed in the automotive business was also marked lower, now projected at ?1% to +1% versus the earlier 1% to 5% forecast.

Near-term production has not escaped disruption. On Tuesday BMW flagged short-term component shortages at external suppliers, which triggered shift cancellations at individual plants. Reuters reported that three factories were affected.

Analysts moved quickly to reprice the stock. Deutsche Bank Research cut its price target to EUR 66 from EUR 71 on 5 November while keeping its "Buy" rating. A day earlier, JPMorgan trimmed its target to EUR 68 from EUR 82, maintaining its "Overweight" stance.

Compounding the operational strain, BMW of North America is recalling 720,796 vehicles in the US over a fire risk tied to a possible short circuit. The NHTSA, the US traffic safety regulator, advised owners to park the affected cars outdoors and away from buildings and other vehicles until repairs are carried out. BMW said the remedy is still being developed.

BMW's Margin Tightrope: Supply Snags, a Cut Guidance and Two Banks Repricing the Stock
sum: BMW is asking investors to weigh two very different kinds of pressure at once. On one side sit the deliberate costs of its restructuring — portfolio and structural measures that pushed the carmaker to slash its 2026 earnings outlook. On the other sit the unplanned headaches: short-term shortages of externally supplied parts that forced shift cancellations at several plants.

The company confirmed the production interruptions in response to a query from Automobilwoche, and media reports named Regensburg, Leipzig and Oxford as the affected sites. BMW said it is working with suppliers on a more stable flow of components and on restarting output, and it has already put measures in place to steady parts procurement. The reports did not specify how severe the stoppages were or which components ran short.

The revised outlook landed on 3 November, when BMW lowered its forecast for the Automotive segment's EBIT margin in 2026 to a range of ?0,5% to +0,5%. The target for free cash flow in the car business — more than €2.5 billion — was left untouched. The company tied the cut chiefly to higher costs for portfolio and structural measures.

That margin corridor is now the central test for the equity story. Even at the top end, the buffer against further setbacks looks thin, which means the operational earnings threshold has become the number to watch.

Third-quarter figures, released on 4 November, put group revenue at €30.5 billion with pre-tax profit of €2.08 billion. The Automotive segment's EBIT margin came in at 3.4%. Alongside the numbers, BMW flagged an accelerated realignment, saying the ramp-up of its New Class models will let earlier vehicle and technology generations be phased out step by step.

There was tangible progress on the supply front too. On Monday the Munich-based group closed additional contracts for Gen6 high-voltage battery cells — with Samsung SDI for Europe and LG Energy Solution for the US. Deliveries from each region are slated to begin in the late 2020s.

Analysts, though, spent the week marking down their price targets. Deutsche Bank Research trimmed its BMW objective from €71 to €66 on 5 November while keeping a "Buy" rating. A day earlier, JPMorgan had cut its target from €82 to €68, maintaining an "Overweight" stance.

BMW Keeps Buying Back Stock While Parts Shortages Test Its Turnaround
sum: BMW's share buyback is running without interruption even as the company works through a production hiccup and a freshly trimmed profit outlook. The Munich-based automaker repurchased 47,159 ordinary shares for EUR 2,772,181.35 last week, according to a Monday announcement detailing its ongoing repurchase program.

The disclosure landed alongside news that shift cancellations have hit three plants. BMW confirmed on Tuesday that short-notice shortages of externally supplied components forced the stoppages, though it declined to identify the missing parts or quantify the production impact. ORF reported that Regensburg, Leipzig and Oxford were affected. Until the company provides figures, the financial cost of the disruption cannot be pinned down.

Earlier in November, BMW lowered its expected EBIT margin for the Automotive segment for the current financial year to a range of ?0.5% to +0.5%, citing expanded portfolio and structural measures among the burdens. Finance chief Walter Mertl put the hit to the segment's EBIT margin from those measures at roughly 2.5 percentage points. Free cash flow in the Automotive segment is still projected at more than EUR 2.5 billion.

The third quarter offered a reminder of the earnings base BMW is working from: a group EBT margin of 6.8% and an Automotive EBIT margin of 3.4%. Deliveries, however, are already trending lower — the group handed over 551,075 vehicles in the quarter, down 6.3% from the same period a year earlier.

How long the parts shortage lasts is now the operative question. A few lost shifts would read very differently from sustained interruptions across multiple sites, and investors will be watching for signals that component supply is normalizing. Reliable day-to-day production matters all the more while the restructuring is under way; repeated stoppages would make the organizational overhaul harder to execute and further cloud visibility.

Analysts have been recalibrating. Deutsche Bank Research cut its price target to EUR 66 from EUR 71 on November 5 while keeping a "Buy" rating, with analyst Tim Rokossa pointing to restructuring measures and limited predictability for 2027. JPMorgan had already reduced its target to EUR 68 from EUR 82 on November 4, maintaining its "Overweight" stance.

BMW's 2026 Guidance Nears Break-Even as Supply Snags Hit Three Plants and S&P Trims Credit Rating
sum: BMW's autumn has turned into a triple squeeze: a profit outlook cut close to the break-even line, a credit downgrade, and now production interruptions at three European plants. The Munich-based automaker confirmed that short-term shortages of supplier parts have forced shift cancellations at its Regensburg, Leipzig and Oxford facilities, according to company sources cited by Reuters. BMW said it is working with suppliers to stabilize parts supply and restart production.
The shares fell 1.3% to €58.28 on the day the plant disruptions surfaced, adding to the previous session's 0.9% decline.

At the heart of the sell-off is BMW's revised guidance. On 3 November the group lowered its 2026 forecast for the Automotive segment to an EBIT margin of ?0.5% to +0.5%, down from the 1% to 3% range it had previously targeted. Segment deliveries are now expected to fall moderately year-on-year.

The third-quarter figures, released alongside the guidance cut, laid bare the pressure. Group revenue slipped 5.8% year-on-year to €30.45 billion, while EBIT dropped 29.7% to €1.59 billion. Net profit came in at €1.45 billion, a decline of 14.7%.
On Thursday, S&P Global Ratings downgraded BMW and its rated subsidiaries to "A-" from "A" on the long-term scale, with the short-term rating moving to "A-2" from "A-1". The outlook is negative.

Analysts responded to the weaker numbers by marking down their price targets while leaving their recommendations untouched. Deutsche Bank Research cut its target to €66 from €71 on 5 November, retaining a "Buy" rating. JPMorgan followed a day earlier, reducing its target to €68 from €82 after the quarterly earnings call while reaffirming its "Overweight" stance.

BMW also announced on 4 November that it will speed up and expand its structural overhaul, with additional restructuring measures and the planned rollout of further Neue Klasse models in 2027. The company cautioned that these measures will weigh on the Automotive segment's result in the fourth quarter of 2026.

BMW's Restructuring Tab Comes Due Just as the Margin Band Touches Zero
sum: BMW shares closed Friday down 3.0%, and the pressure has less to do with the quarter just reported than with the bill arriving next. The Munich carmaker has widened and intensified its portfolio and structural measures, a decision that will land as non-operating charges in the fourth quarter and has already forced it to redraw its profit expectations for next year.

The clearest signal came midweek, when BMW cut its forecast for the Automotive segment's EBIT margin in 2026 to a range of -0.5% to +0.5%. A corridor straddling zero leaves little room for error, and the company pointed squarely at the accelerated overhaul as the reason. For shareholders, the question is no longer whether the weak year was weak — it is whether the extra spending buys a sturdier earnings base on the other side.

Wednesday's release provided the baseline against which that bet will be judged. Group revenues came in at EUR 30,452 million, with group profit before tax of EUR 2,083 million. The operating result fell 29.7% year on year to EUR 1.59 billion, and the Automotive segment's reported EBIT margin stood at 3.4% in the third quarter of 2026 — a figure that now looks generous against the guidance that replaced it.
BMW also flagged continued weakness in China when it presented the quarterly figures, a drag that has not gone away and could yet make even the reduced margin corridor a stretch.

The analyst response on Thursday was uniform in direction and notably restrained in tone. Deutsche Bank Research lowered its price target to EUR 66 from EUR 71 while keeping its buy rating. JPMorgan cut its target to EUR 68 on Wednesday and stuck with its overweight recommendation. The message from both: less upside, same conviction.

That combination — a lower number attached to a positive call — frames the trade-off cleanly. Anyone positioning for a rebound is effectively betting that BMW can hold its reduced expectations, not that it will snap back to earlier levels. A single favourable rating offers no protection if the operating picture keeps deteriorating, and the split among the houses makes the point. Other analysts trimmed their targets to EUR 52 and EUR 56, paired with neutral and reduce ratings respectively. The spread of opinion shows the recovery case is genuinely contested.

sum: Bayerische Motoren Werke reported third quarter 2026 sales of €20,292 million and net income of €1,461 million, alongside a reduced automotive profit outlook and a core margin range that now runs from a slight loss to a slight profit.
The second profit warning of 2026 highlights that weaker China contribution and higher restructuring costs, including workforce reductions, are weighing on BMW's earnings profile.

Bayerische Motoren Werke shareholders effectively need to believe the restructuring and product pipeline can offset weaker China economics and tariff costs. The core short term swing factor is execution on cost cuts while keeping premium pricing power intact. The latest quarter, with lower sales and earnings, puts more pressure on that efficiency story rather than changing it.

The biggest immediate risk still sits in China, where pricing pressure and softer volumes are already visible in the margin reset. Management now signals an automotive margin that could hover around breakeven, so any further demand shock or tariff hit would bite quickly. On the upside, new BEV launches and a leaner cost base remain the main operational catalysts.

The clearest piece of news to track against those catalysts is BMW reaffirming free cash flow guidance above €2.5b and an operational EBIT margin above 2% for 2026, despite lower volume expectations. That indicates management is leaning hard on restructuring, capital discipline and mix, rather than counting on a rapid rebound in unit sales.

sum: BMW Group cut its reported 2026 Automotive EBIT margin outlook to a range of minus 0.5 percent to plus 0.5 percent on Tuesday, November 3, as expanded portfolio and structural measures are expected to weigh on fourth-quarter earnings. The update followed a solid but weaker third quarter, according to the BMW Group.

BMW stock traded at 58.96 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:09 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026, 3.88 percent below the Xetra close of Thursday, November 5. Compared with the 61.22-euro quote at 18:01 CET on November 5 in the previous report, the stock was 3.69 percent lower. The daily comparison uses the Xetra close, while the second comparison measures the move since that report.
The real-time quote of BMW stock reflects the latest Lang & Schwarz trade.

BMW continues to expect the Automotive operating margin before portfolio and structural measures to exceed 2.0 percent in 2026. The reported margin outlook, however, was reduced from the previous range of 1 percent to 3 percent. Automotive return on capital employed is now expected between minus 1 percent and plus 1 percent, compared with the prior range of 1 percent to 5 percent.

The company kept its Automotive free-cash-flow target above 2.5 billion euros. BMW said the additional portfolio and structural measures are expected to reduce the Automotive margin by about 2.5 percentage points in 2026, while the related costs will weigh on the fourth quarter.

BMW delivered 551,075 vehicles in the third quarter, down 6.3 percent year on year, while revenue fell 5.8 percent to 30.452 billion euros. Group net profit declined 14.7 percent to 1.448 billion euros, and the Automotive EBIT margin fell to 3.4 percent.

Demand for Neue Klasse models has prompted BMW to add production shifts and bring forward the phase-out of selected older vehicle and technology generations. Fully electric vehicles accounted for one-fifth of third-quarter sales, while electric vehicles including plug-in hybrids represented 27.4 percent.

sum: Deutsche Bank Research has lowered its price target on BMW from EUR 71 to EUR 66 while keeping its Buy rating intact, according to media reports. Two other research houses also cut their targets following the Munich carmaker's quarterly figures and reduced full-year guidance, with the new marks landing in a EUR 52 to EUR 56 range and carrying "Reduce" and "Neutral" ratings respectively. The spread of recommendations now runs the full spectrum from Buy through Neutral to Reduce.

JPMorgan had already moved the day before, trimming its target from EUR 82 to EUR 68 after the quarterly earnings call while leaving its Overweight rating unchanged. In none of these cases did a lower target come with a downgrade — a distinction that matters for how the recent wave of revisions should be read.

BMW reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of EUR 30,452 million and a pre-tax group result of EUR 2,083 million. EBIT for the quarter came in at EUR 1,589 million, and the EBIT margin in the Automotive segment reached 3.4%. For the first nine months of 2026, pre-tax group profit stood at EUR 6,128 million.

The quarter landed ahead of analyst expectations, and the stock rose yesterday despite the guidance cut — a reaction that pointed to relief over the margin rather than any verdict on the restructuring itself. Shares gained 7.7% in a friendlier sector environment, supported by the broader industry backdrop even as the profit warning hung over the session.

The central question for investors is profitability before portfolio and structural measures, which allows a distinction between the costs of the overhaul and the performance of the running business. Without that separation, a weaker reported margin could be read either too pessimistically or too leniently.

BMW still expects an operating margin above 2.0% for 2026 before those measures. Including the charges, the group on Tuesday cut its guidance for the Automotive segment's EBIT margin to a range of ?0.5% to +0.5%. BMW confirmed that outlook in yesterday's quarterly statement and cited expanded and intensified portfolio and structural measures, along with non-operating charges in the fourth quarter, as the reason for the adjustment.

BMW F 450 RR sportbike revealed
sum: BMW has revealed the F 450 RR, the third motorcycle based on its 420cc engine platform. This follows the F 450 GS, revealed last November, and the F 450 R, which debuted as recently as two weeks ago. This trio of motorcycles is manufactured by TVS in Hosur.
- F 450 RR has the same 420cc engine and chassis as the other two BMW 450s
- Total of three colour options available across four variants
- No prices or an India launch timeline, just like the F 450 R

BMW’s newest offering in its entry-level motorcycle range shares its engine and steel tubular chassis housing the engine as a stressed member, similar to its other two 450s. Its 420cc twin-cylinder liquid-cooled mill continues to mete out 48hp at 8,750rpm and 43Nm at 6,750rpm. Other technical aspects such as the suspension, brakes and kerb weight are closer to its sport-naked sibling, the F 450 R, with sportbike-like design details such as winglets and a full fairing, of course.

The F 450 RR has 17-inch tyres at both ends, KYB-supplied 43mm USD fork and monoshock suspension units, with the latter offering rebound and preload adjustability as standard. The standard seat height is 790mm, and BMW offers two seat options: increase it to 810mm or drop it down to 775mm. Brakes are the same as those on the R: a 310mm front disc with a Brembo four-piston monobloc caliper and a Bybre 240mm rear disc. The base variant of the F 450 RR has a kerb weight of 177kg.

The F 450 RR is available in four variants: Base, Sport, M Sport and M Sport with Innovation Package. As standard, all four get the exact same rider aids as the R, which include dual-channel and lean-sensitive ABS, a 6.5-inch TFT display with smartphone connectivity and three ride modes (Rain, Road and Race). The Base comes in a single Cosmic Black colour. Stepping up to the Exclusive variant gets you the Racing Red colour, a bi-directional quickshifter and Sport suspension that adds rebound and compression adjustability for the USD fork. The M Sport and M Sport with Innovation Package variants give you an additional user-customisable Race Pro ride mode and a Snaefell white/M Motorsport colour scheme; the latter rounds off the package with ERC (Easy Ride Clutch), BMW’s take on clutchless riding that we first saw on the F 450 GS.

BMW's Twin Gambles: A Logistics-AI Bet and a Touchscreen Holdout as the Stock Stays Stuck
sum: BMW is placing two very different bets this week — one on artificial intelligence that could reshape global supply chains, another on a user-interface philosophy that runs against the grain of its German rivals. Neither, however, is moving the needle for investors who remain fixated on the automaker's sagging share price.

The Munich-based company's venture arm, BMW i Ventures, has joined forces with Bosch Ventures, Hitachi Ventures and Yamaha Motor Ventures to back Nauta, a startup building autonomous AI agents for international goods trading. The platform, which describes itself as an operational command center for supply chains, claims to already work with more than 8,000 suppliers across 60 countries. Its client roster includes New Balance, Ashley Furniture, L'Oréal, Modelo and Moët & Chandon — companies that together generate over $50 billion in annual revenue.

Nauta says that in under six months, its software has prevented $3 million in delay-related costs, caught a $300,000 invoicing discrepancy and avoided $1.5 million in inventory outages, all while cutting operational hours per employee by 37 percent. For BMW i Ventures, the investment fits a broader strategy of getting early exposure to technologies promising efficiency gains along the supply chain — a priority that has gained urgency amid persistent global trade disruptions.

In its core business, BMW is charting a course that sets it apart from the rest of the industry. While Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz have been reintroducing physical buttons in response to customer complaints, BMW is doubling down on touchscreens and voice control.

Vikram Pawah, head of BMW Australia, argues that younger buyers — roughly those up to age 45 — are comfortable multitasking and navigate digital interfaces with ease. The upcoming iX3, built on the "Neue Klasse" platform, will largely do away with traditional buttons. BMW points to the 2001 launch of iDrive as evidence of its digital pedigree.

The stance gets complicated by regulatory headwinds in China, where physical controls for functions like turn signals and windshield wipers are set to become mandatory from July 2027. That means BMW will have to adapt its approach in its largest single market, even as it stays the course elsewhere.

BMW Slashes 2026 Profit Outlook, Margin Plunges to 1%-3% as Cost Cuts Accelerate
sum: German luxury automaker BMW Group recently announced a sharp downgrade to its full-year 2026 performance outlook, slashing the automotive segment's full-year EBIT margin guidance to a range of 1% to 3%, down from the previous 4% to 6%. The group also expects full-year pre-tax profit to decline significantly by more than 15%, with core delivery volumes contracting slightly compared to the prior year. The sudden profit warning triggered violent market turbulence, described by analysts as a "wake-up call" for the entire auto industry.

According to an ad-hoc announcement released by BMW Group on the evening of June 16, the core drivers behind the downgrade stem from multiple macroeconomic headwinds. Geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East have pushed up global energy costs and dampened consumer confidence, while tariff factors imposed by various countries are expected to drag down the automotive EBIT margin by approximately 1.25 percentage points. Most critically, the ongoing price war in Asia, particularly in China, continues to compress per-vehicle profitability. Group CEO Milan Nedeljkovic, newly appointed to the role, stated that the company must accelerate structural and efficiency measures to address the "dramatically deteriorating market environment."

Hit by this negative news, BMW shares on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange plunged more than 11% intraday on June 17, ultimately closing down 6.66%. Additionally, shares of OEMs and parts suppliers such as Forvia, Valeo, Renault, and Stellantis also fell in tandem.

The latest financial data shows that BMW's operating conditions had already shown signs of weakness in the first quarter of 2026. Group revenue was 31.01 billion euros, down 8.1% year-on-year; pre-tax profit was 2.348 billion euros, a sharp year-on-year decline of 24.6%; net profit fell 23.1% to 1.672 billion euros. In terms of global deliveries, BMW Group sold approximately 566,000 vehicles in the first quarter, a year-on-year decrease of 3.5%, with battery-electric vehicle (BEV) sales at 87,458 units, a significant year-on-year drop of 20.1%.
The downturn is particularly pronounced in China, BMW's largest single market globally.

Conversion of Preferred Shares into Ordinary Shares: BMW Group Simplifies Capital Structure
sum: Munich. BMW AG is simplifying its capital structure: its share capital of approximately €616 million will in future consist solely of ordinary shares. At today’s Annual General Meeting of BMW AG and a subsequently held separate meeting of preferred shareholders, the conversion of preferred shares into ordinary shares was approved by a clear majority. Approval at the Annual General Meeting amounted to 99,99%, while the separate meeting of preferred shareholders approved the resolution with 99,77%. The conversion will be brought into effect by way of an amendment to the Articles of Association, with no additional payment obligation for preferred shareholders. The conversion will become effective upon registration of the amendment to the Articles of Association in the commercial register. The BMW AG will announce the exact timing by public notice.

Currently, approximately 91% of BMW AG’s share capital consists of voting ordinary shares, and around 9% of non-voting preferred shares, which carry a fixed dividend preference of €0.02 per share. The dividend preference of the preferred shares will be applied for the last time for the 2025 financial year. From the 2026 financial year onward, the balance sheet profit available for distribution will be allocated evenly across all shares. Following the approved conversion at a ratio of 1:1,each share will in future carry the same voting right at the Annual General Meeting.

“For the weighting of BMW AG in major stock indices such as the DAX or the EURO STOXX 50, it is already the ordinary shares that are decisive as the share class with the highest free‑float market capitalization. As a result of the conversion, their proportion in free float will increase significantly by around 19%,” said Chief Financial Officer Walter Mertl on Wednesday in Munich. “This step therefore strengthens the weighting of BMW AG in relevant indices. The simplified capital structure represents a clear added value for investors and may have a positive impact on the share price performance of the BMW share.”

A single share structure follows the internationally recognised corporate governance principle of “one share, one vote”. This increases the attractiveness of the BMW share, in particular for international and institutional investors.

items.t: BMW beats estimates despite profit slump: is the stock a buy now?
sum: BMW stock remained in focus on Wednesday as investors positioned for first-quarter results that delivered a meaningful beat on earnings estimates, even as pre-tax profit plunged by a quarter and revenue fell sharply.

The result confirmed that Europe's premium car industry is absorbing the twin drag of US and EU tariffs and continued weakness in China, but doing so with greater resilience than the market had feared.
That's a combination that has kept BMW's stock above its mid-year lows even as the broader macro backdrop remains challenging.

BMW said on Wednesday that pre-tax earnings came in at 2.3 billion euros — equivalent to approximately 2.7 billion dollars — in the first quarter of 2026, compared with the analyst consensus of 2.2 billion euros compiled by the company.

The result nonetheless marks a steep 25% decline from the same period a year earlier, reflecting the combined impact of lower volumes, tighter pricing in China, and the direct cost of tariffs on vehicles and components flowing between the US, Europe and Asia.

Group revenue fell 8.1% to 31.0 billion euros, while the EBIT margin in the core automotive business stood at 5.0% — above analysts' forecast of 4.7% and comfortably within BMW's full-year target corridor of 4% to 6%.
The margin outperformance is significant given that BMW had flagged tariffs alone would carve 1.25 percentage points from its automotive EBIT margin in 2026.

"The beige life": German woman stunned by Mzansi's fascination with BMWs
sum: - A German woman in an interracial relationship with a South African man shared her thoughts on why South Africans see driving a BMW as the ultimate success
- She explained that in Germany, there is an unspoken social rule about not standing out
- South Africans in the comments had a lot to say, with many laughing at how spot on she was on the local relationship with expensive cars and brands

A German woman living between two very different worlds had South Africans laughing after she posted a video about something she noticed about how people live. She shared her thoughts on her TikTok page @ili_lebo on 4 March 2026, talking about how driving a German car, specifically a BMW, is seen in South Africa as a sign that you have truly made it in life. What amazed her was how different it was from back home, where the very people who build those cars are happily riding the train.

She explained that it goes deeper than just good public transport. In Germany and across much of Northern Europe, there is an unspoken social expectation that you should not stand out. She described it as looking very average on purpose. If you walk into a German mall wearing designer items and flashy jewellery, people do not admire you. Instead, you get what she called "the look". Which is a quiet mix of judgement and discomfort. Her South African boyfriend gave this mindset a name: the beige life.

This way of thinking actually has roots in a broader cultural concept found across Scandinavian and Northern European countries. The idea focuses on not thinking of yourself as better than anyone else, not showing off success and keeping things equal and modest across society. It shapes everything from how people dress to how they behave at work and in public spaces.

sum: BMW Group India reported its highest-ever first-quarter sales in calendar year (CY) 2026, selling 4,567 cars, a growth of 17% year-on-year (y-o-y), even as the broader luxury car market saw moderate performance.

The BMW Future Is Now: An Honest Opinion About the Most Controversial 3er Ever
sum: The same goes for the technology features, as cars today have become personal computers on wheels. BMW is one of the companies that has decided to reinvent itself and step into the unknown. It has a brand new design language called the Neue Klasse, which premiered on the latest iX3, which celebrated its premiere last fall. Fast forward to this week, and the Munich-based auto marque has its second Neue Klasse model.

Christened the BMW i3, it shares nothing but the name with the electric hatch that left the assembly line for good in August 2022, after roughly 250,000 units saw the light of day. Production of this model took place at the Leipzig factory in Germany, whereas the i3 Sedan will enter production at the Munich facility. As its name suggests, this is an all-electric alternative to the future 3 Series, with which it shares very little.

One may have seen some comparisons between the BMW i3 Sedan and the future 3 Series and thought that they are almost identical, but the devil lies in the details. On top of that, the next 3er will utilize an updated version of the CLAR architecture, whereas the modern-day i3 is based on the Neue Klasse platform and shares its nuts and bolts with the iX3. Thus, it is safe to consider it a low-slung alternative to the latest BMW iX3.

Care to discuss the styling? Where, it is basically the thing that defines it. On a positive note, you won’t confuse it for any other Bimmer, for the time being, of course, because the Neue Klasse design language is coming to all future BMW models. The front fascia is said to express a mix between the old days and the modern era. There is a new kidney grille design, which is neatly integrated with the new headlights.

The DRL signature reminds us of certain Peugeots, and there is a generous air intake in the middle of bumper. The hood is now on the small side of things, and hides a small storage compartment below, which is used to store the charging cables. The new BMW i3 Sedan has flush door handles and some very clean lines across the profile. Due to the taillights, the back end is quite XM-ish, and that’s something to think about.
But does it actually look good? To me, it is simply the ugliest BMW 3 Series ever made.

items.t: 2027 BMW i3 'Neue Klasse' EV Sedan Will Help Form the New Heart of the BMW Brand
sum: - The 2027 BMW i3 is a new mid-size electric sedan that shares a newly developed architecture with the BMW iX3 SUV.
- The new i3 is roughly the size of the gas-powered 3-series, but the EV launches with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain that makes 463 hp.
- The i3 is set to go on sale later this year, though BMW hasn't yet released pricing.

BMW's "Neue Klasse" mid-size cars of the 1960s saved the company. Now, BMW is using that term again, this time for a new generation of electric vehicles: the iX3 SUV and the i3 mid-size sedan. Their mission isn't quite as critical as their predecessors', but there's still a lot riding on this latest new class of cars.

The i3 is a nameplate we've seen before—on another pioneering model, a quirky city car offered as a pure EV or with an optional range extender. The new one is unrelated to the previous model. Instead, the model designation identifies it as the EV counterpart to the 3-series sedan, in the same way the i5 is analogous to the 5-series and the i7 to the 7-series. Compared with the current 3-series, the i3 is 1.6 inches longer overall, 1.5 inches wider, and 1.6 inches taller. It sits astride a wheelbase that has grown by nearly 2 inches.

Whereas the i5 and the i7 use the same platform as their gas-engine counterparts, the i3 uses a new platform unrelated to the 3-series. This one, used also by the iX3, features an 800-volt electrical architecture that's capable of ingesting juice at up to 400 kW (should we someday have public chargers that powerful). An NACS port is standard, with CCS compatibility via an adapter. The top AC charger in the U.S. will be a 15.4-kW unit. Its battery pack, which is a structural element in the car, has cells that are 20 percent more energy dense than those in the bigger BMW EVs; total battery capacity is 109 kWh. BMW estimates a maximum range of around 440 miles based on the EPA's testing procedure.

In the i3 50 xDrive model, those cells feed two motors that produce 463 horsepower and 476 pound-feet of torque (output for other i3 models hasn't yet been revealed). The computing power behind the i3 is new as well, consisting of four supercomputers, each controlling a group of functions.

What does McLaren P1 designer Frank Stephenson think of the BMW iX3?
sum: Frank Stephenson is a car designer with more hits than the Beatles, including the Escort RS Cossie, first BMW Mini, Maser MC12, numerous Ferraris and the McLaren P1. These days he runs his own consultancy – Frank Stephenson Design. Here he shares his views on the BMW iX3.

Following its much maligned design direction of recent times, BMW has decided to tone things down a bit. Save for the new/old beaver toothed grille graphic, it’s a welcome departure from what’s gone before. From the front, a conventional ICE-looking lower bumper air intake area appears overly busy for an EV vehicle’s reduced cooling needs.

The new classically proportioned and illuminated kidneys are daintily styled, but too pinched, almost puckered up. The headlamps cleverly create a new lighting signature for the Neue Klasse, the angel eyes now replaced with snake eye graphics.

From the side, large wheels offset the blocky side volume, helping to give an impression of stability. Angled fender creases around the wheel openings are really the only design features in side view that inject any sense of surface entertainment. And yet, they’re a bit visually jarring and don’t quite work with the otherwise subdued side view.

Beyond that, smoothly surfaced body sides and an absence of protruding doorhandles contribute to a very low and respectable 0.24 drag coefficient – great for performance, not so good for visual fanfare.

At the rear, the iX3 has a well planted stance, albeit a bit generic. Long gone are the memorable days of BMW’s signature L-shaped taillights, replaced here with two horizontally positioned units, proudly providing a recessed area for the badge – a similar solution to the bonnet. The registration plate floats below the tailgate within a larger depressed area than needed. This solution stops the flow of the neighbouring surfaces, creating a harshly chiselled zone instead of a smoothly blended in form language.

items.t: Mercedes-Benz India Declines 2.85% In 2025 As BMW Gains Market Share, Highlighting Strategic Shift
sum: After five years of uninterrupted growth, Mercedes-Benz India reported a 2.85 percent year-on-year decline in retail sales in calendar year 2025, delivering 19,007 units compared with 19,565 units in 2024. The contraction marks the company’s first annual volume decline since 2020 and signals that its strategy of prioritising ‘value over volume’ may be eroding its grip on the entry and core luxury segments.

While Mercedes-Benz continues to tout record revenue, driven by high-margin top-end vehicles (TEVs), AMG models, and electric vehicles (EVs), the stark drop in entry-level sales exposes a vulnerability that rivals are increasingly exploiting.

The decline was largely concentrated in the entry luxury portfolio, which fell 20 per cent year-on-year, accounting for only 13 per cent of total volumes. Models such as the A-Class, GLA, and base C-Class variants have struggled to attract first-time luxury buyers, largely due to steep price increases and the absence of aggressive discounting, a deliberate strategy by the German carmaker to protect brand equity.

Meanwhile, the core segment contributed 62 per cent of total sales, and top-end vehicles accounted for 25 per cent. While these figures may sound healthy, the data highlights a skewed portfolio that relies heavily on premium and niche buyers, leaving Mercedes exposed in the high-volume, competitive mid-luxury segment.

Mercedes-Benz’s top-end vehicles, including the S-Class, Mercedes-Maybach, and AMG portfolio, posted 11 per cent growth, with AMG alone surging 34 per cent year-on-year. The EV portfolio grew 12 per cent, and BEVs accounted for 20 per cent of top-end sales, reflecting a clear emphasis on high-ticket products.

However, while these gains support revenue, they cannot compensate for volume losses in the entry segment, where aspirational buyers are increasingly gravitating toward rivals offering better pricing, financing, and newer EV options.

The competitive threat from BMW India is now undeniable. In CY2025, BMW Group India sold a record 18,001 cars, including 17,271 BMW units and 730 MINI cars, representing a 14 per cent year-on-year growth.

Resident shares photo of dangerous sighting along local roadways: 'Sounds like a fire waiting to happen'
sum: A Redditor took to the platform to share a picture of some dangerous litter they found on the side of the road.
Posting in the r/DeTrashed subreddit, the original poster shared a picture of a discarded vape they found by the side of the road.
They found the vape while they were picking up litter. The OP explained that, after searching online, they learned they needed to take the vape to a hazardous waste facility.

"Apparently the lithium battery inside can explode if not disposed of properly," they said in the caption. "I had no idea! I don't mind taking it to one but does anyone know how much I'll be charged?"
Apart from the myriad health concerns that come from vaping, vapes themselves can harm the environment in many ways.

When they're spent, vapes often become litter. Instead of disposing of them properly, people sometimes leave them along trails or in parks. Vapes left on the sides of roads can cause flat tires, leading to much frustration and stress for drivers.
Vapes contain heavy metals like antimony, nickel, and lead. When they're disposed of improperly, those chemicals can leach into the soil and water.
